::: {#rem-estimation-vs-prediction}
#### Estimation versus prediction

Estimation and prediction both measure error as a signed difference,
and both summarize it with a mean squared error
(a pMSE for an estimator, an sMSE for predictions),
but they aim at different targets:

- **Target.**
  An [estimate](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) aims at a fixed, unknown [estimand](estimation.qmd#def-estimand).
  A [prediction](#def-prediction) aims at an outcome $y$,
  which is a random quantity even when the model is known exactly.
- **Error.**
  The [estimation error](estimation.qmd#def-estimation-error) is the estimate minus the estimand.
  The [prediction error](#def-prediction-error) is the prediction minus the outcome.
- **Mean squared error.**
  The [pMSE of an estimator](estimation.qmd#mean-squared-error)
  is an expectation over repeated samples.
  The [sMSE of predictions](#def-prediction-mse)
  is an average over observations.
- **What cannot be removed.**
  The error of a consistent estimator shrinks toward zero as the sample grows.
  A prediction's expected squared error cannot fall below the [irreducible error](model-validation.qmd#def-irreducible-error),
  the variance of the outcome around its conditional mean.

[Validating Predictions](model-validation.qmd) estimates the prediction error on new observations.
:::
